description: Converting complex numbers between algebraic form (a+ib) and trigonometric form r(cos theta + i sin theta), including products/quotients in trig form and using trig form to compute powers.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, trigonometric-form conversion exercises spanning two scanned volumes (continuous question numbering) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = 1+i
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta), r=|z|, theta=arg(z)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = 1-i\sqrt{3}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = -\sqrt{3}+i
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = -\sqrt{6}-i\sqrt{2}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = 3i
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta), purely imaginary

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form: } z = -6i
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta), purely imaginary

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z = 4\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{5}+i\sin\frac{3\pi}{5}\right) \text{ and } w = 2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{5}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{5}\right). \text{ Write } zw \text{ and } \frac{z}{w} \text{ in trigonometric form, then deduce the modulus and an argument of each.}
exercises.technique: product/quotient of complex numbers in trig form (r1 r2, theta1+theta2; r1/r2, theta1-theta2)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z = \dfrac{\cos\frac{4\pi}{9}+i\sin\frac{4\pi}{9}}{\cos\frac{\pi}{9}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{9}} \text{ in trigonometric form and in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: quotient of complex numbers in trig form, then convert to algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = 1+\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}+i\sin\frac{2\pi}{7}
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = \sin\frac{2\pi}{5}+i\left(1-\cos\frac{2\pi}{5}\right)
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = \sqrt{2+2\cos\frac{4\pi}{9}}+i\sqrt{2-2\cos\frac{4\pi}{9}}
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = \sin\frac{4\pi}{5}+i\left(1+\cos\frac{4\pi}{5}\right)
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = 1+i\tan\frac{4\pi}{5}
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the following complex number in trigonometric form (find its modulus and an argument): } z = 1+i\cot\frac{4\pi}{7}
exercises.technique: trig form via half-angle/sum-to-product identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=\frac{1}{2} \text{ and } \arg(z)=\frac{\pi}{3}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=3\sqrt{2} \text{ and } \arg(z)=\frac{\pi}{4}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=8, \arg(z)=\frac{\pi}{6}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=4, \arg(z)=\frac{2\pi}{3}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=2, \arg(z)=-\frac{\pi}{2}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z \text{ in algebraic form given: } |z|=4\sqrt{2}, \arg(z)=-\frac{\pi}{4}
exercises.technique: z = r(cos theta + i sin theta) -> algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z = (\cos x+\sin x)+i(\cos x-\sin x),\ x\in\mathbb{R}. \text{ Show that } |z|=\sqrt{2} \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}.
exercises.technique: compute |z| = sqrt(a^2+b^2) and simplify using cos^2+sin^2=1

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Prove the identities: } a)\ \cos x+\sin x=\sqrt{2}\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-x\right) \text{ for all } x\in\mathbb{R}; \quad b)\ \cos x-\sin x=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-x\right) \text{ for all } x\in\mathbb{R}.
exercises.technique: trigonometric addition formulas

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z = (\cos x+\sin x)+i(\cos x-\sin x) \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: trig form using identities from part b

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z=1+i\tan\theta \text{ and } w=1+i\cot\varphi \text{ where } 0<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2} \text{ and } 0<\varphi<\frac{\pi}{2}. \text{ Calculate } |z| \text{ and } |w|.
exercises.technique: |z| = sqrt(a^2+b^2) with tan/cot

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z, w, wz \text{ and } \frac{z}{w} \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: trig form, product and quotient in trig form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the complex number } z=\dfrac{1+\sin\alpha+i\cos\alpha}{1+\sin\alpha-i\cos\alpha} \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: trig form via conjugate multiplication and trig identities

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } a=-2+2i \text{ and } b=1+i\sqrt{3}. \text{ Write } z=a^2+b^2-2b+3 \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: complex arithmetic in algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } a, b, ab \text{ and } \frac{a}{b} \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: trig form, product and quotient in trig form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z=\sqrt{2}+i\sqrt{2} \text{ and } w=2\sqrt{3}+2i. \text{ Write } \frac{z}{w} \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: complex division, algebraic form

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z, w \text{ and } \frac{z}{w} \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: trig form of z, w and quotient

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Deduce that } \cos\frac{\pi}{12}=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4} \text{ and } \sin\frac{\pi}{12}=\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.
exercises.technique: compare algebraic and trigonometric forms of z/w to identify cos(pi/12), sin(pi/12)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } Z = 1+\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}+i\sin\frac{2\pi}{7}. \text{ Write } Z \text{ and } Z^4 \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: Use sum-to-product / half-angle identities to write 1+\cos\theta+i\sin\theta in trig form, then apply De Moivre's formula for Z^4.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } Z = \sin\frac{\pi}{10}+i\cos\frac{\pi}{10}. \text{ Write } Z \text{ and } (1+Z)^4 \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: Convert sin/cos-swapped form to standard cos+i\sin form via complementary angle identities, then combine with 1+Z and apply De Moivre's formula.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } a=2\sqrt{3}+2i \text{ and } b=2-2i. \text{ Write } Z=a^2+b^2-4a+4\sqrt{3}b \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Direct algebraic expansion and simplification of complex expressions.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } a=2\sqrt{3}+2i \text{ and } b=2-2i. \text{ Write } a, b, \text{ and } ab \text{ in trigonometric form.}
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of each given complex number; modulus/argument of a product multiply/add.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write the complex number } A = \frac{2(1+i)^2}{1-i\sqrt{3}} \text{ in trigonometric form, then in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Convert numerator and denominator to trig form separately, apply De Moivre for the square, divide (subtract arguments), then convert back to algebraic form.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } Z = (\sqrt{2}-i\sqrt{2})\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6}-i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right). \text{ Write } Z \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Multiply a number in algebraic form by a number in trig (negative-angle) form, expand and simplify.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } Z^2 \text{ in trigonometric form, where } Z = (\sqrt{2}-i\sqrt{2})\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6}-i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right).
exercises.technique: Convert Z to trig form and apply De Moivre's formula for the square.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Using the previous results, calculate } \cos\frac{5\pi}{12} \text{ and } \sin\frac{5\pi}{12}.
exercises.technique: Equate the algebraic-form and trig-form representations of Z^2 obtained above, and read off cosine/sine values by comparison.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Calculate the modulus and an argument of } w = \left(\frac{1+i\sqrt{3}}{1-i}\right)^{20}.
exercises.technique: Convert numerator and denominator to trig form, divide (subtract arguments, divide moduli), then apply De Moivre's formula for the power.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } Z = \sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1} + i\sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}. \text{ Show that } Z^2 = 2+2i.
exercises.technique: Direct squaring and simplification of a nested-radical complex expression.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } Z^2 \text{ and } Z^{4038} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } Z^2=2+2i.
exercises.technique: Convert Z^2 to trig form, then apply De Moivre's formula to obtain Z^{4038}=(Z^2)^{2019}.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } Z^{4038} \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Reduce the angle of Z^{4038} modulo 2\pi and convert the resulting trig form back to algebraic form.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } u=-1-i\sqrt{3} \text{ and } v=\sqrt{3}+i. \text{ Write } z = u^2+v^2+|uv| \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Expand squares and modulus of a product, then combine and simplify algebraically.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Calculate the modulus of } z, \text{ where } z=u^2+v^2+|uv|, u=-1-i\sqrt{3}, v=\sqrt{3}+i.
exercises.technique: Compute |z| = sqrt(a^2+b^2) from the algebraic form found in the previous part.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } u \text{ and } v \text{ in trigonometric form, where } u=-1-i\sqrt{3}, v=\sqrt{3}+i.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of each given complex number.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } u=1+i \text{ and } v=\sqrt{3}+i. \text{ Write } z = u^2+v^2+4u-2iv \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Direct algebraic expansion and simplification of complex expressions.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Calculate the argument of } z, \text{ where } z=u^2+v^2+4u-2iv, u=1+i, v=\sqrt{3}+i.
exercises.technique: Determine \arg(z) from the algebraic form a+ib found in the previous part.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } u, v, uv, \text{ and } \frac{u}{v} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } u=1+i, v=\sqrt{3}+i.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus/argument of u and v individually, then combine (multiply moduli/add arguments for uv; divide moduli/subtract arguments for u/v).

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z = \frac{1+i\sqrt{3}}{1+i}. \text{ Calculate } z \text{ and } z^2, \text{ writing each in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate to simplify the quotient, then square the result and simplify.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z^2 \text{ and } z^{4038} \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z = \frac{1+i\sqrt{3}}{1+i}.
exercises.technique: Convert z^2 to trig form and apply De Moivre's formula to obtain z^{4038}=(z^2)^{2019}.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Determine the smallest positive integer } n \text{ such that } z^{2n} \text{ is a real number, where } z = \frac{1+i\sqrt{3}}{1+i}.
exercises.technique: z^{2n} is real when n times the argument of z^2 is a multiple of \pi; find the smallest positive integer n satisfying this.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Let } z = \sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}} + i\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}. \text{ Calculate } z^2 \text{ and } z^4, \text{ writing each in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Direct squaring of a nested-radical complex expression, then squaring again.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Write } z^2 \text{ and } z^4 \text{ in trigonometric form, where } z = \sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}} + i\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}.
exercises.technique: Compute modulus and argument of z^2, then apply De Moivre's formula to obtain z^4.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find real numbers } p \text{ and } q, \text{ knowing that } z^2 \text{ and } z^4 \text{ are roots of the quadratic equation } x^2+px+q=0.
exercises.technique: Use Vieta's formulas: p = -(z^2+z^4) and q = z^2\cdot z^4, computed from the algebraic-form values found above.
